body:
Found by playing the **pointer-drag route on the real map** — the route the owner actually uses, and the least tested one. Almost every playtest so far went through coordinate entry because it is easier to script; the one bug that genuinely blocked the owner (#493) also lived here and was invisible from the other route.

## What a player sees

Mid-drag on a wall run, if the button's release is never delivered to the page as an explicit `pointerup`, **the wall ghost does not go away**. It keeps following the cursor and recomputing the run — the count and direction change on every hover — while the player is no longer holding anything and believes they are just looking around.

Nothing wrong is ever *built*: a later fresh press-and-release places exactly one correct wall, because `beginBuild` resets unconditionally. But a preview saying "a wall is about to appear here", driven by nothing, is precisely what gets reported as "the game glitched". Only Escape clears it.

## The cause, stated separately from the measurement

`commitBuild` / `finishPointer` fire only from Phaser's `'pointerup'` and `'pointerupoutside'` (`src/rendering/scene/world-scene.ts:461-472`). Nothing watches a plain `'pointermove'`'s `buttons` bitmask for a release that never arrived explicitly.

**This repository has already paid to fix this once.** Issue #202 measured 1,419 world units of runaway panning from a key held down when focus left the window, and added a `window` `blur` handler. That handler calls **`this.keyboard.releaseAll()` and nothing else** (`world-scene.ts:348-350`).

The three pointer gesture state machines — `buildPointerId`, `areaPointerId`, `objectPointerId` (`world-scene.ts:229-261`) — are structurally identical to each other and have **no equivalent recovery**. The same gap #202 closed for the keyboard, left open on three sibling fields.

## Evidence, reproduced twice independently

- Armed the wall tool, pressed and dragged to a ghost of `3 × North from 16, 16`. Dispatched a real `window` `blur` — ghost unchanged, exactly as the code predicts. Then a `mouseMoved` carrying `buttons: 0` with **no `mouseup` or `pointerup` ever dispatched**. The ghost stayed frozen through two further no-button moves. A subsequent fresh press-and-release built exactly one new wall, `Brick wall · 12, 13 · North` — no corruption, no doubling.
- Same setup, then **an ordinary hover with the button genuinely up**: the ghost changed to `3 × North from 14, 16`, then `2 × West from 16, 16`. `extendBuild` was still matching the stale `buildPointerId` and recomputing the run against the *original* press anchor, live, on plain hover. `Escape` cleared it — proving `buildPointerId` had genuinely stayed set, since `cancelBuild` (`world-scene.ts:791-798`) is the only thing that reaches it.

## What is not known, stated rather than glossed

**Whether a real desktop browser ever delivers exactly that sequence** — a `buttons: 0` move with no prior `mouseup` — is engine- and OS-dependent, and the literal "alt-tab away and release over another window" case is not testable from here: Playwright's virtual mouse has no OS focus to leave.

What *is* certain, from reading the code rather than inferring it: **no path in `WorldScene` would recover from it if it does happen.** That is a real gap regardless of how often the trigger fires, and it is the same gap the `blur` handler exists to close.

**The room and object tools were not independently reproduced.** Their `cancel*`/`extend*` pairs are the same shape as the build tool's, so the same gap is expected — but that is inference from reading, explicitly not something that was run.

## Everything else in the pointer route matched its preview

Recorded so it is not re-litigated. All verified by execution against the real app, with queue rows read **structurally** (they are pooled and `hidden`, so `textContent` reads dead rows):

- Wall runs — straight, reversed, and diagonal dominant-axis-picking — each committed exactly the run its ghost showed.
- **Release over a HUD panel button** committed the previewed run and did *not* trigger the button underneath: pointer capture decides the release, not whatever element is under the cursor. Correct.
- **Release beyond the viewport edge** (y = −80) committed exactly the ghost, via `pointerupoutside`.
- **Wheel-zoom mid-drag** did not corrupt the run; continuing afterwards extended it correctly at the new scale.
- **Middle-button pan while armed** panned and placed nothing.
- **A second room drag without confirming** fully *replaced* the pending rectangle rather than merging — area readout and confirm label both changed, exactly as `rooms-panel.ts` promises.
- Every too-small, not-enclosed and "must stand in a zoned room" refusal came back with a specific correct reason, never a silent failure.
- The **bed's 1×2 footprint ghost** draws 1 wide and 2 tall, anchored top-left and growing down, matching `footprintRectAt`.

## Reached only halfway, and flagged rather than guessed

Whether the bed's press **actually claims those two tiles** was not established. It needs an enclosed zoned room, which needs walls to finish *construction* rather than merely be queued, and materials delivery consumed most of a simulated day at 1× — the orders sat in `Awaiting Materials` throughout. A real cost of the scenario, not a defect.

## Suggested shape

Wire `blur` to cancel the build, room and object gestures the same way it already releases the keyboard — and, if a `pointerup` can genuinely go missing, also treat a `pointermove` observed with `buttons === 0` as a release. The three state machines are identical, so whatever is done should be done to all three at once rather than to the one that was reproduced.
title: A pointer gesture stays open when the release never arrives — #202's blur fix covers the keyboard and not the three drag state machines
